en: The Jātaka:
The Sixth Book, the Chapter on the Unobstructed (Avāriyavagga)
6. The Migālopajātaka “I do not like the deer’s flesh,
since such is your destiny.”
You fly, dear one, to what is not yours;
you frequent, dear one, that which is not your domain,
like a field with four corners.
When the earth comes to an end for you,
then, dear son, turn back;
do not go further than this.
“There are other birds as well,
winged creatures that travel through the air;
they too are carried away by the force of the wind.”
Gone are those eternalist views.
Having failed to carry out the instruction of your father Apananda, who was advanced in years;
Having passed beyond the Kālavāta winds,
he entered the realm of the Verambha winds;
his sons and wives [remained behind].
And all those others who lived under him met with ruin,
for they did not offer counsel to the brahmin.
So too, here in this world,
he who does not understand the words of the elders is one who wanders beyond the boundary, intoxicated with pride.
Their teaching has been devoured by vultures;
failing to act upon the instruction of the Elder, they all fall into calamity.
The Migālopa Jātaka is the sixth.
